title.title: The Correspondence of the Yarnall family

msIdentifier.institution: Friends Historical Library of Swarthmore College

projectDesc.p: The correspondence of the Yarnall family is stored at the Friends Historical Library of Swarthmore College. With the generous support of H. David and Joyce E. Hunt, Library staff scanned and transcribed these letters in 2024 and encoded the text in TEI.

div.p: I should earlier than this have given thee a few lines in compliance with thy dear Husband’s request & my own inclination, but indisposition has prevented until now. I was favored to reach my own home last second day. When I left Newport, thy Peter (who had been my fellow laborer through all the families of professors there) was in good health, and intended that day to set off, taking the meetings on the way to Nantucket from whence I expect he has returned & is industriously filling up his duty towards Boston. He has been much owned in his religious services, & his company truly acceptable to me & to Friends generally. I trust, my dear Friend, thou wilt be supported in faith & patience during his absence, & therein reap the reward intended alike for those who stay by the stuff, as for those who go forth in battle, & that in the Lord’s time thy dear partner will be restored to thee with sheaves of unifying peace + which is also in measure, my present comforting experience.

closer.salute: With the salutation of sisterly love, I remain thy assured & affectionate Friend,
